survey: A handheld calculator floats tilted against a flat orange background, its face angled toward the camera. It has one rounded navy body; the left and bottom edges show its thickness. A blank pale display panel sits flush in the upper face. A small red key (power or clear) sits on the top rim above the display, on the body. Below the display is a 4×4 key grid. The three left columns are navy keys, 12 in all, which is enough for the digits and a few functions. The right column holds four larger cyan operator keys. Every key is a raised rounded block on the face, spaced evenly, so each could be pressed. The rows and columns follow the body's tilt and perspective throughout. The display has no digits, which is a normal simplification. There are no loose parts, nothing passes through anything else, and the object is plainly a calculator that could work. It floats, but as a standalone icon on a flat background, not resting on a surface.
